memories.content: The user keeps a small table fan beside the bedroom window.
On a day the user drank coffee late in the afternoon, they could not fall asleep until dawn.
On a day the user drank coffee before 2 p.m., they fell asleep at their usual time.
On a tired day, the user ate dinner out and postponed even washing the dishes after returning home.
In the same week, on a day the user made simple noodles at home, they rested immediately after the meal.
On a night the window was left open, street noise woke the user twice.
On a night the table fan was running, the user was not too warm even with the window closed.
The user's father prefers to have coffee available after dinner and believes it will not cause a sleep problem.
When making a sleep-related suggestion, do not treat one or two records as a general lifestyle habit.
The user tends to go to bed much later after drinking coffee late in the afternoon.
The user keeps four folding chairs for family barbecues in storage.
When six family members gathered in a noisy indoor restaurant, the user asked several times for the person across from them to repeat what was said.
The user held the next gathering in their father's yard and moved between seats while speaking with everyone.
On a day the user started the barbecue at midday, sunlight led them to finish the meal quickly.
The next time, the user started at 6 p.m. and remained outside until sunset.
Because the side dishes brought by the user's mother and older sister had no labels, the user opened the same container twice.
At the next gathering, the user wrote each food's name and who brought it on a small piece of paper.
After a barbecue, the user's younger brother prefers to divide leftover food into small containers to take home rather than discard it.
The local agent can summarize preparation and responses from prior family barbecues but cannot know the next attendees or weather.
The user's father's yard receives strong direct sunlight at midday; after 6 p.m., shade and wind lower the felt temperature.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate domains: the reference records sleep, coffee timing, bedroom conditions, meals, and inference caution, while the compared frame records family-barbecue logistics, environmental timing, food handling, conversation conditions, and forecasting limits. No cross-frame operational claim materially overlaps or conflicts.
